lines: Ro co-founder and CEO Zach Reitano argues the core flaw in US healthcare is that patients are rarely the real customer, and that cash-pay, direct-to-consumer models where patients control the transaction deliver better quality at lower cost.

He casts GLP-1 drugs as an upstream intervention against the leading causes of death, moving healthcare from reactive chronic-disease management toward prevention; the show notes Ro grew from a $250M to over $3B run rate in four years with fewer staff than in 2021.

Reitano credits that efficiency to sequencing initiatives one at a time rather than in parallel, and says stagnation comes from confusing long-term vision with near-term strategy, which bloats headcount and can demand a radical reset.
He describes a 'strong attract, strong repel' culture with explicit operating principles to keep top talent and quickly remove misalignment.
He also argues social stigma signals latent unmet demand that marketing can unlock, and calls protecting existing roles over safer, superior technology a moral error.
podcast: Invest Like the Best with Patrick O'Shaughnessy
title: Zach Reitano - Building Ro and Why Healthcare Should Be 50% of GDP - [Invest Like the Best, EP.500]
